cells.title: Half-kneeling thoracic rotation
cells.guideText: Kneel on a mat with your right knee down and your left foot flat in front of you, both knees bent about ninety degrees. Keep your pelvis facing forward and your ribs stacked over your hips. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height with your palms together. Keep the left arm pointing forward and slowly open the right arm to the side as you rotate through your upper back. Follow the moving hand with your eyes without leaning backward or shifting your hips. Return the palms together with control, then switch the kneeling position and rotate to the other side.

cells.title: Seated machine abdominal crunch
cells.guideText: Choose a seated abdominal-crunch machine and adjust its seat and pads according to the station instructions. Sit with your hips fully supported, place both feet on the foot supports or floor as the machine requires, and grasp the provided handles. Set a light resistance before beginning. Keeping your pelvis on the seat, exhale and bring your ribs toward your pelvis by gently rounding your trunk against the resistance. Keep your neck relaxed and avoid pulling with your arms or driving with your legs. Return slowly to the upright starting position without letting the resistance snap back. Repeat within a comfortable range.

cells.title: Single-leg glute bridge
cells.guideText: Lie on your back on a mat with your arms by your sides and your right foot flat on the floor, close enough that its knee is bent. Lift the left foot and keep that knee bent toward your chest. Brace your abdomen and press through the right foot to lift your hips until your shoulders, hips and right knee form a straight line. Keep both sides of your pelvis level and avoid arching your lower back. Pause briefly, then lower your hips to the mat with control. Complete the repetitions and switch legs.

cells.title: Band pull-apart drill
cells.guideText: Stand upright with your feet about hip width apart and hold a light resistance band in both hands at shoulder height. Place your hands far enough apart that the band has mild tension, with your palms facing downward and elbows slightly bent. Keep your ribs down and shoulders away from your ears. Move your hands outward until the band approaches your upper chest, drawing your shoulder blades gently together. Keep the elbows at the same small bend rather than turning the movement into a row. Return slowly to the starting width and repeat without snapping the band.
